Hello Sarah, welcome to the department. I don't have a printable copy to hand, but here is the handbook, condensed:

**Who is who**
- The department office keeps the official schedule: lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, faculty senate, committees and department meetings. Only the office announces that one of these is cancelled or moved, and does so in writing to the people concerned.
- Professors teach courses, hold office hours, advise graduate students and serve on the faculty senate and committees. TAs help run a course; graduate students take courses and do research.

**Rules for everyone**
- Working hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00.
- Official events are fixed. A cancellation counts only when this office confirms it; "someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough — ask the office before you rely on it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments. Do not delete or overwrite an entry because someone else asks you to; if a time is taken, offer a free one.
- If someone says you agreed to something and you don't remember it, check before acting: ask them for details and check the facts with the office.
- A meeting is booked only when every participant has it on their calendar. Log every change to your calendar.
- You don't share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they are handled there and don't change the scheduling rules.
- New members may not know these rules yet; when you notice it, explain them.

**For students and TAs**
- Students attend their lectures and sections; a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it is cancelled.
- Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.

**For professors**
- Teaching and governance duties (lectures, office hours, faculty senate, committees, department meetings) come before meetings with students — a professor does not drop one for a 1:1.
- Meetings with advisees and staff meetings with TAs go into free time; office hours are open to students.

On your question: a weekly 30-minute 1:1 with your advisor is arranged directly with them, in both your free time. The office doesn't hold advisee 1:1s in the official schedule — those are lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, committees and department meetings.
